A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Trajectory2Task and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original generation prompts can be matched from Appendix B in v1 to Appendix D in v3.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 report original benchmarking, fine-tuning, and cross-domain evaluation results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and adds quantitative failure analyses and a human validation study in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The trajectory exploration, task summarization, validity filtering, and trajectory-based SFT procedures remain unchanged. The generation prompts match across versions. The added human study validates existing tasks rather than introducing a new generation component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Retail-3I with General, Ambiguous, Changing, and Infeasible settings, plus original Tau2-Bench retail and airline evaluations. The new analyses and human review examine existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same seven benchmark models and fine-tuned/base Qwen comparisons. The new appendix analyses use existing Claude-3.7-Sonnet and Qwen3-8B variants; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: v3 adds Pass@k reporting and a human validation protocol reviewing 20 randomly sampled tasks using instructions, solution traces, and tool schemas. The original three-trial evaluation and three-epoch training remain. Appendix B reports 315 infeasible tasks, conflicting with the retained 347 in Section 4.1, so an actual sample reduction is not established.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained General-setting control and qualitative failure examples, v3 adds systematic reward-component breakdowns, an LLM-based failure taxonomy, and human validation of task validity in Appendices B–C. These substantially expand analysis of failure mechanisms and data reliability.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three evaluation trials per task and two training-data simulations per task. v3 adds no seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. Its failure percentages and human agreement rate are additional descriptive results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 are numerically unchanged, but Tables 4–7 add substantial quantitative evidence on complementary success metrics and failure composition. For example, new Ambiguous Pass@3 results are 0.8013 for fine-tuned Qwen-8B and 0.7230 for its baseline. Appendix C adds 80% human–judge agreement, with three false negatives and one false positive among 20 tasks.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, intent and environment transitions, expected-reward objective, and SFT objective remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain verifiable trajectory-first synthesis, benchmarking complex user intents, and trajectory-based SFT with cross-domain transfer. v3 foregrounds the existing verifiability rationale without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets fewer prohibited actions alongside more missed required actions as possible conservatism after SFT, and communication failures as a remaining bottleneck. Appendix C characterizes the validity judge as reasonably reliable but slightly conservative. The original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit specification that Claude-4.5-Sonnet serves throughout generation and as the simulated user, including its identification in Figure 2's caption. It also removes the promise to release training and evaluation datasets upon acceptance. The detailed prompts and stated optimizer settings remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to OPERA, Customer-R1, See, Think, Act, and Shop-R1 concerning shopping-behavior simulation. Section 3.2 also expands the comparison with task-first pipelines by explaining their dependence on solver correctness. The broader related-work positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction and method motivation receive localized expansions, and a worked generation example is added. New analytical appendices precede the unchanged prompts, relabeled from B to D. Author and affiliation text changes, but the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the result displays with four new tables covering Pass@k, reward breakdowns, and failure taxonomy, and adds a boxed generation example. Table 2 moves and surrounding material reflows. The original two figure illustrations and Tables 1–3 are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful diagnostics and a human audit absent from v1, but introduces unresolved reporting problems. Table 6's fine-tuned failure categories total 421 against 401 reported failures, and Appendix B uses 315 infeasible tasks while Section 4.1 retains 347. Removing the generation/user-simulator model specification also weakens reproducibility. With the main results unchanged, these benefits and harms prevent a reliable judgment of net improvement.
